newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index hits record on HSBC gains.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index hits record on HSBC gains.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index roared to a record high on Tuesday gaining 200 points to an all-time high of 16,460 within the first few minutes of trade, as HSBC shares surged on the bank's results.
"The bank's results were above expectations so the stock has moved up more than it lost yesterday," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
HSBC shares were up HK$9.00 at HK$273.00 after falling HK$4.00 ahead of its earning's announcement on Monday.
The banking giant announced a 13 percent rise in pretax profit for the first six months of the year to 2.62 billion sterling.
Au-Young said it was difficult to say where the Hang Seng Index was heading after it burst into record ground on Tuesday.
"We are in a major bull run. 16,500 is not the limit but may be initial resistance," said Au-young.
The Hang Seng Index extended early gains to hit an all-time high of 16,482.74 before paring gains to trade up 156 points, or 0.96 percent, at 16,416 after the first 20 minutes of trade.
Shares in Cheung Kong rose HK$0.50 to HK$88.00 and Hutchison Whampoa rose HK$0.25 to HK$77.75.
Jardine Matheson Ltd and Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday that Cheung Kong and Hutchison had bought shares in both companies.
"Although for the time being we do not know their intention, this represents a good opportunity for them," said Au-Young of Cheung Kong and Hutchison.
"They should know if this is a profitable investment."

Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.50 to HK$110.50 after posting a 14.5 percent rise in interim net profit to HK$4.98 billion. "Most of the market's gains are in HSBC and the rest of the market is lagging," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. He said he was surprised that the strength of the rally had fizzled so rapidly.
